title: Commonly Confused Words
description: Word pairs that blur together, each asked in the sentence that settles it.

cards.front: The new policy will ___ morale. (affect / effect)
cards.note: Affect is the verb, effect is the noun — the policy affects morale and has an effect on it.

cards.front: One immediate ___ of the change was confusion. (affect / effect)
The dog wagged ___ tail. (its / it's)
cards.note: It's always means "it is" or "it has". The possessive its has no apostrophe.

cards.front: ___ going to rain. (its / it's)
The ___ of the school greeted us. (principal / principle)
cards.note: The principal is your pal (a person, or the main thing); a principle is a rule.

cards.front: Honesty is a matter of ___. (principal / principle)
The medicine had no ___ on the fever. (affect / effect)
___ cars on the road. (fewer / less)
cards.note: Fewer counts things you can count; less measures what you cannot — fewer cars, less traffic.

cards.front: ___ noise after midnight. (fewer / less)
The award will go to ___ deserves it. (whoever / whomever)
cards.note: The clause needs a subject: whoever deserves it. Whomever is only ever an object.

cards.front: Please ___ the invitation. (accept / except)
cards.note: Accept is to receive; except is to leave out.

cards.front: Everyone came ___ Nia. (accept / except)
The climbers began their ___ of the peak. (ascent / assent)
cards.note: Ascent is the climb; assent is the agreement.

cards.front: She nodded her ___. (ascent / assent)
The road runs ___ the river. (past / passed)
cards.note: Passed is only ever the verb pass in the past tense; everything else is past.

cards.front: The runner ___ the finish line. (past / passed)
Take my ___: study early. (advice / advise)
cards.note: Advice is the noun (say -ice like mice); advise is the verb (say -ize).

cards.front: I would ___ you to back up your work. (advice / advise)
The data ___ a trend, whatever we conclude. (imply / infer)
cards.note: The speaker or the data imply; the listener infers.

cards.front: From her tone, I ___ she disagreed. (imply / infer)
She is taller ___ me. (then / than)
cards.note: Than compares; then orders events in time.

cards.front: Finish this, ___ rest. (then / than)
The ship was ___ in the storm. (stationary / stationery)
cards.note: Stationary stands still (a is for at rest); stationery is paper (e is for envelope).

cards.front: The shop sells ___. (stationary / stationery)
